articles.headline: Breaking: FDA approves groundbreaking pancreatic cancer drug
articles.summary: The FDA approved Revolution Medicines' Rasonque (a RAS(ON) inhibitor) for advanced pancreatic cancer approximately 6.5 months ahead of its PDUFA date, marking the first approval in a new class of KRAS-targeted therapies. The pivotal trial showed the drug nearly doubled overall survival versus chemotherapy. The monthly list price of ~$39,800 exceeded Wall Street consensus, prompting upward revisions to peak sales estimates.
articles.why_it_matters: RVMD receives a major de-risking catalyst with above-consensus pricing and an accelerated approval timeline, making near-term launch execution and peak sales trajectory the central investment question for the stock.

articles.headline: Nvidia Climbing the Wall of Worries
articles.summary: MBI Deep Dives unpacks Nvidia's latest earnings, noting that FY2028 sell-side revenue estimates were off by ~$400B just a year ago, and that management's ~70% guided growth may represent a floor given supply constraints. The piece dissects a key tension: Nvidia is actively cultivating neoclouds to commoditize hyperscalers, while hyperscalers are simultaneously the primary customers filling neocloud backlogs — a structural risk if hyperscalers close the capacity gap. Despite staggering operating outperformance, NVDA has barely outperformed the S&P 500, reflecting a buy-side skepticism that the stock must 'climb the wall of worries' to re-rate.
articles.why_it_matters: For investors, the article reframes NVDA not as a momentum trade but as a structural thesis stress-test — the neocloud dependency, frontier lab concentration risk, and margin sustainability questions are the real valuation variables that will determine whether the stock catches up to its fundamentals.

articles.headline: Where AI agents pay off: A practical guide to the economics of agentic workflows
articles.summary: McKinsey presents a practical economic framework for evaluating where AI agentic workflows generate measurable ROI versus hype, examining task complexity thresholds, human-in-the-loop cost structures, and industry-specific deployment patterns. The piece is forward-looking and rigorous, aimed at enterprise decision-makers assessing autonomous AI agent adoption. It has particular relevance to biopharma and health systems navigating AI investment decisions.
articles.why_it_matters: This framework equips investors to distinguish which AI-in-drug-discovery and health tech companies have durable economic moats from those selling commodity automation — directly actionable for portfolio positioning in the AI-healthcare intersection.
